title: Grade 3 Science — Mon, May 25
description: Plants — Parts and Functions — Day 1 of 5
subject: science

questions.question: Which part of the plant soaks up water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil and anchor the plant firmly.

questions.question: What do leaves make for the plant?
questions.explanation: Leaves make food for the plant through photosynthesis, using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What is the main job of the stem?
options: Carry water and food between roots and leaves
questions.explanation: The stem supports the plant and carries water (from roots) and food (from leaves) to all parts.

questions.question: Plants make their own food using:
questions.explanation: Plants make food (glucose) using sunlight, water from roots, and carbon dioxide from air — this process is called photosynthesis.

questions.question: What do we call the coloured part of a flower?
questions.explanation: Petals are the colourful parts of a flower that attract insects for pollination.

questions.question: Which gas do plants release into the air during the day?
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, plants release oxygen into the air — which is the oxygen we breathe!

questions.question: Seeds grow inside:
questions.explanation: After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into a fruit which contains seeds.

questions.question: What type of plant has no seeds and reproduces through spores?
questions.explanation: Ferns are non-flowering plants that reproduce through spores, not seeds.

questions.question: Which part of the plant makes new plants through seeds?
questions.explanation: Flowers are the reproductive part of the plant. They produce seeds after pollination.

questions.question: A cactus stores water in its:
questions.explanation: A cactus stores water in its thick, fleshy stem — this helps it survive in dry deserts.

questions.question: What do you call plants that lose their leaves in autumn?
questions.explanation: Deciduous plants shed their leaves in autumn and winter. Examples: oak, maple.

questions.question: Why do plants need sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sunlight provides the energy plants need to make food (glucose) through photosynthesis.

questions.question: What is germination?
options: Seed sprouting and beginning to grow
questions.explanation: Germination is when a seed starts to sprout and grow into a new plant, given warmth, water, and air.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a plant?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms are fungi, not plants. They don't have roots, leaves, or make food through photosynthesis.

questions.question: What are the green things inside a leaf that help make food?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll — the green pigment that captures sunlight for photosynthesis.
